name: Muscat–Singapore
why: Restores a direct Oman–Singapore link and strengthens Gulf–Southeast Asia connectivity.

name: Riyadh–Kuala Lumpur
why: Adds Saudi Arabia’s new flag carrier into the Gulf–Malaysia corridor.

name: Riyadh–Mumbai
why: Riyadh Air’s first India route adds premium capacity on a major India–GCC business corridor.

name: Abu Dhabi–Tashkent
why: Creates a daily UAE–Uzbekistan link and a new Etihad gateway into Central Asia.

name: Changchun Metro Line 7
why: Adds a major orbital/cross-city corridor and expands Changchun’s metro network.

name: Riyadh–Bangkok
why: Strengthens the fast-growing Saudi–Thailand tourism and business corridor.

name: Shanghai Pudong–Manila
why: Adds a new Chinese carrier on one of the key China–Philippines trunk markets.

name: Changsha Metro Line 2 Phase 2
why: Extends Line 2 northwest and expands Changsha’s rapid-transit reach toward the future HSR interchange.

name: Mumbai–Hanoi
why: Akasa’s Vietnam entry adds a fourth nonstop operator pattern on Mumbai–Hanoi ahead of IndiGo’s planned daily service.

name: Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2
scale: 11 km · 11 stations; network now ~17 km / 16 stations
why: Moves Indore Metro beyond its initial demonstration section into major residential and commercial districts.
source: PIB: inaugurated 5 Sep; passenger service from 6 Sep 2026

name: Riyadh–Manila
why: Adds substantial new Gulf–Philippines capacity serving VFR, labour and business traffic.

name: Thailand tourist visa-exemption overhaul
scale: 30-day visa exemption for 60 countries/territories; 15-day exemption for 2; VoA reduced to 3
why: Materially changes short-stay access to Thailand across India, Japan, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and West Asia source markets.

name: Jakarta LRT Kelapa Gading–Manggarai
why: Connects North/East Jakarta directly into Manggarai’s major multimodal rail hub.

name: Xiamen Metro Lines 4 & 6 public trial
scale: Line 4 ~45 km; Line 6 trial section 28.3 km
why: Major expansion of Xiamen’s orbital/cross-bay network; Line 6 is Fujian’s first cross-city metro link into Zhangzhou.
source: Public trial began 16 Sep 2026; not yet treated as formal revenue opening

name: Boten–Vientiane C95/C96 morning service
scale: C95 Boten 08:00 → Vientiane 11:47; C96 Vientiane 14:05 → Boten 18:32; 6 stops
why: Adds same-day north–south travel options along the China–Laos rail corridor via Luang Prabang and Vang Vieng.

name: Kathmandu–Shanghai
scale: Direct scheduled service · frequency not stated in launch release
why: Reopens a direct Nepal–Shanghai corridor; Himalaya says it will be the only scheduled nonstop carrier on the route.

name: Delhi–Hong Kong
scale: Daily · A321XLR through 24 Oct; A321neo from 25 Oct
why: Restores a major India–Hong Kong nonstop corridor after the Jul–Sep temporary suspension.

name: Kolkata–Shanghai Pudong
scale: Daily service restored after Jul–Sep suspension
why: Re-establishes a key eastern-India link to mainland China and improves Kolkata's role as an India–East Asia gateway.
source: IndiGo: temporary suspension ended 30 Sep; bookings/service resumed from 1 Oct 2026

name: Bali (Denpasar)–Phuket
scale: Daily · A320 (174 seats); increased from 4× weekly
why: The move to daily service materially improves direct connectivity between two major Southeast Asian leisure hubs without a Jakarta/Kuala Lumpur/Singapore connection.
source: Route launched 9 Sep 2026; increased 4× weekly → daily from 3 Oct 2026

name: Riyadh–Mumbai
why: Adds low-cost Saudi capacity on a major India–GCC business, VFR and labour corridor.

name: Air India Express Winter 2026 network expansion
scale: 40+ new routes phased from 25 Oct; major additional West Asia and Southeast Asia capacity
why: Represents a broad step-up in Indian short-haul international capacity, especially on Gulf and Southeast Asian corridors.
source: Air India Express winter schedule coverage: announced 6 Oct 2026

name: Kuching–Jakarta
scale: Direct service targeted for end-Oct 2026 · ~1h30 block time; frequency not yet stated
why: Adds a direct Sarawak–Jakarta link and supports Kuching's push to become a stronger ASEAN regional gateway.
source: Sarawak Premier / DayakDaily: end-Oct launch reconfirmed 6 Oct 2026

name: Mumbai international slot-shift plan
operator: MoCA / MIAL / Navi Mumbai International Airport
scale: Proposed shift affected 265 of 770 weekly international departures; 25 Oct implementation deferred
why: Avoids an immediate one-third reduction in Mumbai international departure slots while airlines and airport operators negotiate a transition plan.
source: MoCA / Business Standard / Indian Express: deferment announced 6 Oct 2026

name: Thiruvananthapuram–Riyadh
why: Adds another direct South India–Saudi link and strengthens Kerala–GCC connectivity.

name: Thiruvananthapuram–Bahrain
why: Adds direct capacity from Kerala to Bahrain for VFR, labour and business traffic.

name: Istanbul–Chengdu Tianfu
scale: 3× weekly · B787-9; inaugural flight scheduled B777-300ER
why: Adds Turkish Airlines’ first western-interior China gateway and strengthens China–West Asia/Europe transfer options.

name: Almaty–Tokyo Narita
why: Creates a rare nonstop Japan–Central Asia link and strengthens Almaty's role as a regional transit hub.
source: Air Astana / AeroRoutes: starts 30 Nov 2026; Mon/Thu outbound

name: Taipei–Delhi
why: Restores EVA Air passenger service to India and adds a Taiwan-based nonstop option linking Delhi with Taipei and onward East Asia/North America connections.
